purpose: Create review-stage Design and Challenge candidates only for thin published reasoning cells, using source-supported routes without forcing them through the Diagnose failure-mode generator.
boundary: These are authored review-stage candidates. They are not referenced by case-sets.json and cannot become published cases without a separate human promotion decision.

design: State the business decision and operating constraints.
Compare at least two viable process or architecture alternatives.
Assign decision and state ownership for each alternative.
Explain integration, data, operational, and financial consequences.
Name trade-offs and at least one condition that would change the choice.
Define evidence that would validate the design after implementation.
challenge: State the proposal or assumption being challenged.
Separate the attractive benefit from the hidden dependency or risk.
Compare at least two alternative control models.
Explain authority, failure, recovery, and observability boundaries.
Name conditions under which the original proposal becomes acceptable.
Define evidence and evaluation criteria for the decision.

gap_plan.note: The evidence-backed RAW-MCP candidate survived semantic review. No second Diagnose candidate is needed until the first human promotion decision is made.

candidates.title: Choose the supply model for a new customer offering
candidates.prompt: A company launches a configurable product with uncertain demand. Some customers need short lead times, some orders require customer-specific production, and an external supplier can also deliver the product. Design the sales-to-supply model. Compare sell-from-stock, make-to-order, and third-party supply before selecting the default and exception paths.
expected_points: Start from customer promise, demand variability, customization, stock risk, and supplier capability rather than from a sales document type.
Compare sell-from-stock, make-to-order, and third-party supply as different ownership models for inventory, supply execution, and customer commitment.
Explain which master-data and process decisions must distinguish the variants and where Sales hands responsibility to Production or Procurement.
Include ATP/customer-promise implications, billing path, inventory ownership, and the financial consequence of the selected supply model.
Define a default model plus explicit exception criteria instead of forcing every order through one variant.
Name the trade-off between response time, working capital, customization, supplier dependency, and process complexity, then state what condition would change the choice.
follow_up_questions: What would make you move a product from make-to-order to stock-based fulfillment?
Which responsibility remains with Sales in a third-party flow even when Procurement owns supplier execution?
red_flags: Chooses a process variant from SAP familiarity before stating the business operating model.
Treats third-party, make-to-order, and stock sales as document-type differences only.
Does not state what condition would change the design.
candidates.novelty_note: Published Sales Design practice currently focuses on ownership in a third-party delay. This candidate instead tests deliberate selection among competing sales-to-supply operating models.

candidates.title: Challenge an autonomous-agent proposal for a mostly deterministic SAP process
candidates.prompt: A team proposes an autonomous agent for an SAP exception process. Most steps are deterministic, but a minority require reading unstructured context and choosing among controlled actions. Challenge the proposal. Compare deterministic workflow, a bounded agent, and a more open-ended agent, then define the architecture you would accept.
expected_points: Separate deterministic process control from the small part that actually needs probabilistic reasoning.
Compare workflow, bounded-agent, and broader-agent options by task variability, side-effect risk, latency, auditability, and recovery needs.
Keep business authority, user/agent identity, backend authorization, tool scope, and final transactional state outside model discretion.
Prefer a mixed architecture when deterministic controls can own approvals, writes, and recovery while the agent handles interpretation or option generation.
Define trajectory and business-outcome evaluation, observability, fallback, and post-action verification before increasing autonomy.
State what evidence or change in process variability would justify moving to a more autonomous design.
follow_up_questions: Which failure cost would make you reduce autonomy even if task success is high?
When is an agent unnecessary even if the model can technically perform the task?
red_flags: Calls agents more modern and treats that as an architecture argument.
Moves deterministic approvals or authorization into prompt instructions.
Evaluates only the final answer and ignores trajectory, side effects, and business state.
candidates.novelty_note: Published AI/Data Challenge practice compares retrieval with fine-tuning. This candidate challenges autonomy level and deterministic-versus-agent control boundaries instead.
